provenance.note: Curated compilation; per-record citations carry the accountability. Indian Kanoon is the mirror used for court orders; the court and case number are the citation.

payload.note: Ahmedabad's lake record is a municipal programme with a court docket beside it. AMC's budgets count 176 lakes and report progress on each; the Gujarat High Court's 2002 directions on gazetting and protecting water bodies, and its 2025 orders upholding the clearance of lake land, set the legal frame. Where AMC's budget and the AMRUT 2.0 portal disagree on the same lakes, both are stated.

projects.scope: AMC counts 176 lakes within its limits. By February 2026 development was complete at 43, under way at 13, and planned at 22 more: 15 new lakefronts and 7 re-developments or second phases (Budget 2026-27, PDF p.166). The work covers deepening, compound walls, roads, gardens, lighting, inlets, toilets, recharge wells and bringing catchment water in (PDF p.165). In its 2020-21 budget AMC counted 122 lakes (PDF p.138); the budgets we read do not say what changed between the two counts.
projects.funding_summary: Stated programme cost Rs 100.00 crore (PDF p.165). Shakri lake completed at Rs 17.50 crore; Makarba, Hebatpur and ABD Kachariyu lakes under way at Rs 19.72 crore from AMC's own funds (PDF p.166). Planned: 15 lakefronts at Rs 80.00 crore and 7 re-developments at Rs 40.00 crore (PDF p.166), and gardens at 24 lakes at Rs 51.00 crore (PDF p.181). The English climate annex groups the planned lakefronts as 21 lakes, a different list (PDF p.321).

projects.scope: Storm-water lines that carry rain from each lake's surrounding catchment into the lake. Of 176 lakes, the network is complete at 80, under way at 51, and planned at the remaining 45 (Budget 2026-27, PDF p.166; English climate annex, PDF p.321).
projects.funding_summary: Rs 10.00 crore for catchment-to-lake works in 2026-27 (PDF p.166).

projects.financier: AMRUT 2.0, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
projects.scope: Eight AMC projects on the AMRUT 2.0 portal, Rs 63.02 crore in all. Completed: Ognaj village lake (Rs 8.60 crore), Okaf (Rs 12.74 crore) and Bhadaj (Rs 7.93 crore). Contract awarded: Ropda (Rs 3.76 crore), Vadu at Ramol (Rs 10.13 crore), a mini STP at Asarwa lake (Rs 9 crore), Muthiya (Rs 6.05 crore) and Hathijan (Rs 4.81 crore).
projects.funding_summary: Portal figures as read on 14 October 2026; the portal dates no project. AMC's 2026-27 budget (February 2026) gives different figures for the same lakes: Bhadaj and Okaf under way at Rs 24.92 crore combined, Hathijan and Naroda-Muthiya under way at Rs 15.61 crore, and Ramol Vadu and Ropda under way at Rs 20.47 crore (PDF p.165). Its English annex lists Bhadaj, Ognaj and Okaf as work in progress (PDF p.323). Both are stated here.

projects.financier: Government of Gujarat, Swarnim Jayanti Mukhya Mantri Shaheri Vikas Yojana
projects.scope: Sola, Shilaj, Lal Bahadur Shastri (Malek Saban) and Gota (phase 1) lakes developed and complete; Mumatpura lake under way at Rs 5.54 crore (Budget 2026-27, PDF p.165). The English annex names Jagatpur and Mumatpura as SJMMSVY lake works in progress (PDF p.323).
projects.funding_summary: Rs 63.88 crore for the four completed lakes. The 2025-26 budget listed Shakri in the same Rs 63.88 crore group, then in progress (PDF p.196); the 2026-27 budget lists Shakri separately, completed at Rs 17.50 crore.

projects.scope: Phase 1 beautification in Danilimda ward, under way at Rs 36.38 crore in both the 2025-26 (PDF p.196) and 2026-27 budgets (PDF pp.102 and 166). Phase 2 is planned for the coming year (PDF p.104), with a lake garden at Rs 4.50 crore (PDF p.181).
projects.funding_summary: Phase 2 is Rs 40.00 crore in the South zone works list (PDF p.104); the lake section lists it inside a seven-lake group whose total is also Rs 40.00 crore (PDF p.166). Both are stated; the budget does not reconcile them.

projects.financier: National Disaster Mitigation Fund through NDMA (15th Finance Commission), with a State share
projects.scope: New lake interlinking in the South West zone, Rs 76.00 crore and 24% complete, and in the East zone, Rs 78.00 crore and under way (Budget 2026-27, PDF p.133).
projects.funding_summary: The 2026-27 budget gives the city's grant as Rs 250.00 crore from the Centre and Rs 25.00 crore from the State, and its total as Rs 270.00 crore (PDF p.133). The 2024-25 budget gives the same two parts and a total of Rs 275.00 crore (PDF p.138).

projects.scheme_name: Planned lake interlinking, North West zone
projects.scope: Linking 6 lakes in Town Planning Schemes 217, 41 and 301 and pumping their storm water to the Gota-Godhavi canal, Rs 40.00 crore; and a line from Rajathal through Chebli lake to Bopal lake, Rs 8.00 crore (Budget 2026-27, PDF p.166).

projects.scheme_name: Housing linked to clearing lake land
projects.scope: Of the 24,000 homes AMC plans to build, 3,200 are listed under removing encroachments from lakes, which the budget classes as untenable slums (Budget 2026-27, PDF p.190).
projects.funding_summary: Rs 410.00 crore in the 2026-27 budget. The 2025-26 budget gave about 4,000 homes at Rs 600.00 crore for the same purpose (PDF p.215).

projects.scope: Rebuilding the lake's edge and precinct as a public lakefront, begun in 2006 (Budget 2026-27, PDF p.176). HUDCO's compendium describes a 2.25 km pedestrian promenade and notes the lake 'represented a source of aquifer recharging'.
projects.funding_summary: About Rs 36 crore (AMC Budget 2026-27, PDF p.176); Rs 36.00 crore (HUDCO Best Practice Awards compendium, p.34).

projects.financier: Proposed: Government of India 60%, Government of Gujarat 40%
projects.scope: In 2020 AMC counted 122 lakes, 26 developed and 96 still to be developed, and submitted a Rs 452.90 crore DPR for 45 of them to the Gujarat Urban Development Mission under the National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Ecosystems: 17 lakes over 5 hectares in phase 1 (Rs 310.59 crore) and 28 lakes of 2.5 to 5 hectares in phase 2 (Rs 142.31 crore) (Budget 2020-21, PDF p.138).
projects.funding_summary: Centre Rs 271.74 crore, State Rs 181.16 crore (PDF p.139). The same budget's opening note says 28 lakes had been developed, not 26 (PDF p.4). The 2023-24 budget planned Jagatpur lake and a 2 MLD STP under the NPCA grant (PDF p.147).

court_orders.case: Shailesh R. Shah v. State of Gujarat, (2002) 3 GLR 447
court_orders.ruling: directed the State to notify every lake and pond in Gujarat in the Official Gazette within three months and keep them as water bodies, never alienated; to prescribe and monitor water-quality standards; to rejuvenate them through a declared, phased desilting programme with storm-water recharge; to set up a Water Resources Council and Committee; to record and remove encroachments in accordance with law and the Government's rehabilitation policies; and to determine and notify a no-construction belt around each lake.
court_orders.concern: the protection of lakes in and around Ahmedabad and the removal of encroachments from survey no. 353

court_orders.case: Fuljaha Noormohammed Shaikh and others v. State of Gujarat and others
court_orders.ruling: refused to stay the clearance of structures at Chandola Lake, holding that 'Chandola Lake is a water body and on a water body, no construction can be permitted', and left the petitioners free to apply individually for housing under the State's rehabilitation schemes. It disposed of the petition on 24 July 2025, recording that the demolition had been carried out. The 29 April order's text is as quoted in the Court's judgment of 16 March 2026 in R/SCA 2301/2026, which the link opens.
court_orders.concern: the clearance of homes on the lake land before any rehabilitation

court_orders.case: Samsuddin Jainulabiddin Shaikh and others v. State of Gujarat and others
court_orders.ruling: rejected the prayer to halt the clearance until the petitioners were rehoused, no document having been produced to justify the structures on lake or government land, and directed that individual applications for alternative housing under the State's rehabilitation scheme be considered in accordance with law.
court_orders.concern: the clearance of homes near the lake before rehabilitation

court_orders.case: In re: news item on water bodies vanishing in Ahmedabad
court_orders.court: National Green Tribunal, Western Zone Bench
court_orders.ruling: added the State's Urban Development and Urban Housing Department and AMC as respondents and asked them to reply within four weeks, after the Gujarat Pollution Control Board said it held no specific details of the water bodies identified in the city and pointed to the High Court's 2002 directions. The matter was next listed for 22 January 2026.
court_orders.concern: a newspaper report of 9 June 2025, on which the Tribunal registered the case, that by a civic body report some of Ahmedabad's water bodies had 'vanished'

court_orders.case: Navneetlal Vanmalidas Khakhkhar (Thakkar) and others v. Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation
court_orders.ruling: upheld AMC's notice of 8 September 2025 to remove structures from the lake land, holding that construction on a water body is contrary to the Gujarat Land Revenue Code, 1879. A Division Bench dismissed the appeal on 2 December 2025 and declined to stay the notice.
court_orders.concern: a notice to vacate homes and a temple on lake land that the Collector allotted to AMC in 2009 for development and beautification

court_orders.case: Ashokbhai Kanjibhai Chavda and others v. Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation and others
court_orders.ruling: dismissed the challenge to AMC's notices of 6 November 2025 to vacate structures on revenue survey no. 258, holding that no construction is permissible without permission on government land or a water body, and left the petitioners free to apply to AMC for rehabilitation under any available scheme.
court_orders.concern: AMC notices, issued on a State Government direction to develop and beautify the pond, to clear homes from the pond land
